summary: As of Thursday, October 1, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq setup is balanced between a powerful AI/semiconductor earnings signal and a still-difficult rates backdrop. The Nasdaq Composite finished Wednesday up 0.24% at 26,861.06 after being up as much as 1.2% intraday, helped by softer-than-expected PCE inflation and gains in Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia. Early Thursday Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures were about 0.3% higher. The softer inflation print cut the market-implied probability of an October Fed hike to roughly 38%, which is supportive for growth valuations, but the 10-year Treasury yield has pushed to about 5.31%, its highest since June 2007, so the long-duration valuation pressure has not gone away.

Micron delivered a strong fundamental read-through for the AI complex after the close: quarterly revenue and adjusted profit beat estimates, first-quarter revenue guidance of $61.5 billion was well above the roughly $57.0 billion consensus, and customer commitments under long-term supply agreements rose to $32 billion. Yet Micron shares rose less than 1% in extended trading and the results failed to generate a broad risk-on response in Asian AI shares, suggesting much of the AI-demand strength may already be reflected in positioning. Oil is another two-sided input: Brent was near $98.15 after rising more than 14% in September, while U.S.-Iran talks continue through Qatari mediation. Any credible de-escalation would ease an important inflation/yield pressure point; renewed friction could quickly reverse that relief.

events.title: 1. Initial jobless claims — 8:30 ET
events.detail: The weekly labor-market reading matters mainly through Treasury yields and Fed expectations. After Wednesday's softer inflation reduced October hike odds, a surprisingly strong claims reading could reintroduce rate pressure, while evidence of cooling labor demand would reinforce the case for patience from the Fed ahead of Friday's payroll report.

events.title: 2. ISM Manufacturing PMI — 10:00 ET
events.detail: This is the day's main scheduled macro catalyst. The September manufacturing report can move both growth expectations and the rates market; the Nasdaq-friendly combination would be resilient activity without a renewed inflation signal, while a strong prices component or unexpectedly hot activity could push long yields higher again.

events.title: 3. Micron earnings read-through for semiconductors
events.detail: Micron's results strongly validated AI-memory demand, with revenue, profit and forward guidance above expectations and substantially larger customer commitments. The key market test today is whether that fundamental strength broadens into NVDA and the semiconductor complex rather than remaining largely priced into MU. A muted semiconductor response despite the earnings beat would be an important sign of near-term saturation or consolidation risk.

events.title: 4. U.S.-Iran/Hormuz diplomacy and oil
events.detail: Iran has received U.S. feedback on its proposed seven-day trust-building plan through Qatari mediators, but sequencing remains unresolved. With Brent still near $98 after a 14% September rise, credible progress toward reopening normal Hormuz traffic could relieve inflation and Treasury-yield pressure; a breakdown or renewed military escalation would be an immediate Nasdaq headwind through oil and rates.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the constructive scenario is Micron's AI-demand validation pulling semiconductor leadership higher while the 10-year yield stops advancing and oil remains contained; that combination would give the modest futures gain much better internal confirmation. The downside scenario is more subtle: if semiconductors cannot respond to an unusually strong Micron report while the 10-year holds around or above 5.30%, it would suggest that good AI fundamentals are increasingly being offset by valuation and extension pressure. The 8:30 ET claims release can move rates first, but 10:00 ET ISM is the more important scheduled test; oil and U.S.-Iran headlines remain capable of overriding both.
